topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets out the course context, and outlines the learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Cancer etiology: intrinsic factors versus environmental exposures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce cancer development as an evolutionary genetic process shaped by endogenous cellular errors, genetic predisposition, and environmental exposures reflected in epidemiological data.

topics.label: Pathogens and infectious agents in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how viral, bacterial, and parasitic infections drive cancer development, with a detailed focus on the etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical and physical carcinogenesis and tumor promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how direct and indirect mutagens, metabolic activation, radiation, tissue and life-stage susceptibility, and tumor promoters contribute to cancer formation.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and testing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the analytical, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro experimental strategies used to determine whether agents cause cancer.

topics.label: Lecture closing and risk-benefit considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic delivers the closing remarks, framing cancer prevention and exposure in terms of everyday risk-benefit decisions.
